intro.title: Build versioned APIs v1 and v2 with compatibility
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Node.js API that supports two versions (v1 and v2) of an endpoint, allowing older clients to keep working while new features are added. You will learn how to use Express.js routing to create versioned API paths, such as '/api/v1/data' and '/api/v2/data'. The core concept is API versioning, which helps maintain compatibility as your application evolves. You'll work with basic JavaScript functions, Express middleware, and JSON responses to return different data structures for each version.
intro.usecase: Versioned APIs are essential for maintaining and evolving web services without breaking existing clients. In real-world applications like e-commerce platforms, a v1 API might handle basic product listings and checkout, while a v2 API introduces new features like personalized recommendations or advanced payment methods. This pattern ensures that mobile apps or third-party integrations using the older API continue to function seamlessly, while new features are rolled out in v2. Developers implement this in Node.js to support long-term compatibility, similar to how social media platforms gradually update their APIs to add new data fields or endpoints without disrupting legacy integrations.
